facts.statement: Lewisuchus was a genus of archosaurs that lived during the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: Lewisuchus is a genus of archosaur that lived during the Late Triassic (early Carnian).

facts.statement: Lewisuchus possessed osteoderms, or bony armor, along its back.
facts.quote: It exhibited osteoderms along its back.

facts.statement: Fossils of Lewisuchus have been found in the Chañares Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the Chañares Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: The first remains of Lewisuchus were discovered during a 1964–1965 joint expedition by the Museo de La Plata and Harvard's Museum of Comparative Zoology.
facts.quote: The first remains of Lewisuchus were discovered in a 1964-1965 joint expedition by the Museo de La Plata and Harvard's Museum of Comparative Zoology.

facts.statement: Alfred Romer named the genus Lewisuchus in 1972 based on a partial skeleton catalogued as 64-XI-14-14.
facts.quote: Alfred Romer named Lewisuchus as a new genus in 1972, based on the partial skeleton which at that point was stored at the Museo de La Plata with catalogue number 64-XI-14-14.

facts.statement: The genus name Lewisuchus honors Arnold D. Lewis, the preparator who discovered the holotype skeleton.
facts.quote: The generic name honored Arnold D. Lewis, the chief preparator who discovered the skeleton while working on the recovered nodule.

facts.statement: A 2010 study suggested that Pseudolagosuchus major and Lewisuchus admixtus are the same species, both being basal members of the family Silesauridae.
facts.quote: A 2010 study in the Journal Nature by Nesbitt et al. also made a case for their synonymy, as they were approximately the same size, came from the same locality and strata, and both were found to be basal members of the recently named family Silesauridae.

facts.statement: A 2014 study refrained from synonymizing Pseudolagosuchus major with Lewisuchus admixtus due to insufficient overlapping fossil data.
facts.quote: However, Bittencourt et al.'s 2014 redescription of the Lewisuchus holotype refrained from synonymizing the two due to a lack of data, with the only overlapping material being the tibia and a few cervical (neck) vertebrae.

facts.statement: A new specimen discovered in 2013 and described in 2019 provided evidence that Pseudolagosuchus major and Lewisuchus admixtus are the same species.
facts.quote: A new specimen of Lewisuchus discovered in 2013 was described by Martin Ezcurra et al. in 2019, helping to settle the synonymy debate.

facts.statement: Lewisuchus is classified within the family Silesauridae.
Lewisuchus lived between 241.464 and 233.6 million years ago, spanning the Ladinian to Carnian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Ladinian to Carnian (241.464 to 233.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Lewisuchus was a silesaurid dinosauriform, a group of reptiles considered to be the closest relatives of dinosaurs.
rejected.quote: As a silesaurid dinosauriform, it was a member of the group of reptiles most commonly considered to be the closest relatives of dinosaurs (possibly true dinosaurs themselves).
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'considered to be the closest relatives of dinosaurs'
